chapters.title: Renal Anatomy and Physiology Relevant to Acute Kidney Injury
chapters.description: Structure and function of the kidney with emphasis on glomerular and tubular microanatomy, renal microcirculation, and mechanisms that determine glomerular filtration and urine formation, providing the physiological basis for understanding acute kidney injury (AKI) and recovery potential.
subtopics: Gross renal anatomy and blood supply (renal artery, interlobar, arcuate, cortical and medullary microcirculation)
Glomerular structure: endothelium, basement membrane, podocytes and mesangium
Peritubular capillaries and vasa recta
Mechanisms of glomerular filtration and autoregulation
Tubular epithelial cell physiology and solute transport
Oxygen delivery, susceptibility to ischemia, and mechanisms of acute tubular necrosis (ATN)
Renal handling of water, electrolytes and acid–base
Pathophysiologic responses to injury: inflammation, fibrosis and repair
Clinical correlates: markers of kidney function (creatinine, BUN), urine output interpretation

chapters.title: Pathophysiology of Sepsis and Septic Shock
chapters.description: Host–pathogen interactions and systemic responses that characterize sepsis, mechanisms driving distributive shock, multiorgan dysfunction, metabolic derangements, and immune dysregulation.
subtopics: Definitions: infection, sepsis, severe sepsis, septic shock (Sepsis-3 criteria)
Innate immune activation: pattern-recognition receptors, cytokine storm
Microcirculatory dysfunction, endothelial activation and glycocalyx shedding
Coagulation–inflammation cross-talk and propagation of organ injury
Cardiovascular effects: vasodilatation, capillary leak, septic cardiomyopathy
Metabolic consequences: lactic acidosis, hypoglycaemia in sepsis
Immunoparalysis and secondary infections
Clinical markers and prognostic scoring (qSOFA, SOFA)
General principles of supportive care in sepsis

chapters.title: Hemostasis, Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation (DIC) and Laboratory Interpretation
chapters.description: Physiology of the coagulation cascade, platelet function, fibrinolysis and the pathogenesis, clinical features and laboratory diagnosis of DIC and related coagulopathies.
subtopics: Overview of coagulation pathways (intrinsic, extrinsic, common) and regulators
Platelet function and primary hemostasis
Fibrinolysis and its regulation
Pathogenesis of DIC: causes, microthrombosis and bleeding
Laboratory tests: PT/INR, aPTT, fibrinogen, D-dimer, platelet count, peripheral smear
Interpretation patterns in DIC versus other coagulopathies
Clinical manifestations and complications (bleeding, organ ischemia)
General management principles and indications for blood product support

chapters.title: Thrombotic Microangiopathies (TMA): Classification and Clinical Approach
chapters.description: Overview of TMAs as a group of disorders characterized by microangiopathic hemolytic anemia, thrombocytopenia and organ ischemia; classification into TTP, typical HUS (STEC-HUS), complement-mediated HUS and secondary TMAs, with diagnostic algorithms and initial management strategies.
subtopics: Defining features of TMA and common clinical presentations
Classification: thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP), Shiga toxin–associated HUS, complement-mediated HUS, secondary TMAs (drugs, pregnancy, malignancy, infections)
Diagnostic workup: peripheral smear, schistocytes, hemolysis labs, ADAMTS13 activity, stool tests for Shiga toxin, complement studies
Clinical scoring tools (PLASMIC score) and triage while awaiting tests
Organ-specific manifestations (renal, neurologic, cardiac, skin)
Prognostic factors
General therapeutic principles and urgency of interventions

chapters.title: Complement System: Pathways, Regulation and Laboratory Assessment
chapters.description: Detailed examination of the complement cascade (classical, lectin, alternative pathways), key regulatory proteins, mechanisms that restrict complement activation to pathogens, and laboratory assays used to evaluate complement activity in disease.
subtopics: Components and activation cascades of the classical, lectin and alternative pathways
Formation and function of C3 convertases, C5 convertase and the membrane attack complex (MAC)
Regulatory proteins: factor H, factor I, factor B, membrane cofactor protein (MCP/CD46), decay-accelerating factor (DAF/CD55), complement receptor 1
Consequences of uncontrolled complement activation on endothelium
Laboratory tests: C3, C4, CH50, AH50, functional pathway assays, detection of factor H autoantibodies
Pre-analytical and post-treatment effects on complement assays (plasmapheresis, complement inhibitors)
Interpretation pitfalls and clinical correlations

chapters.title: Complement-mediated Hemolytic Uremic Syndrome (CM-HUS): Mechanisms and Management
chapters.description: Pathogenesis of CM-HUS as a disorder of dysregulated alternative pathway activation, genetic predisposition and common triggers, diagnostic criteria, and evidence-based treatment options including complement blockade.
subtopics: Mechanistic overview: alternative pathway dysregulation leading to endothelial injury and TMA
Genetic contributors: pathogenic variants in CFH, CFI, CFB, C3, MCP (CD46) and their penetrance
Acquired mechanisms: anti-factor H autoantibodies
Common triggering events: infections, pregnancy, medications and transplant
Diagnostic considerations: exclusion of STEC-HUS and TTP, role of complement testing and genetics
Therapeutic strategies: supportive care, plasma exchange/plasma infusion, indications for complement inhibitors (eculizumab and newer agents)
Monitoring, duration of therapy and factors guiding discontinuation
Prognosis and long-term renal outcomes

chapters.title: ADAMTS13 Biology and Thrombotic Thrombocytopenic Purpura (TTP)
chapters.description: Function of ADAMTS13 in von Willebrand factor processing, pathophysiology of TTP due to severe ADAMTS13 deficiency, laboratory testing, and specific acute therapies.
subtopics: Structure and function of von Willebrand factor (vWF) multimers and ADAMTS13 metalloprotease
Mechanisms of ADAMTS13 deficiency: congenital mutation versus acquired autoantibodies
Clinical syndrome of TTP: pentad concept and organ involvement
Laboratory assessment: ADAMTS13 activity assays, inhibitor testing, platelet count and hemolysis markers
Urgent management: plasma exchange, corticosteroids, caplacizumab and immunosuppression
Differentiating TTP from other TMAs

chapters.title: Hematology: Microangiopathic Hemolytic Anemia (MAHA) and Laboratory Markers
chapters.description: Mechanisms and laboratory diagnosis of MAHA and other hemolytic processes, interpretation of hemolysis markers, and the role of immunohematology testing.
subtopics: Pathophysiology of mechanical RBC destruction in MAHA
Laboratory markers: hemoglobin, reticulocyte count, LDH, bilirubin (indirect), haptoglobin, peripheral blood smear
Schistocytes: formation, quantification and differential causes
Direct antiglobulin test (DAT/Coombs): indications, interpretation and causes of false positives
Distinguishing autoimmune hemolytic anemia from MAHA and other causes
Transfusion considerations in hemolysis

chapters.title: Renal Pathology of Thrombotic Microangiopathy
chapters.description: Histopathological features of TMA in the kidney across acute and chronic stages, correlation of light microscopy, immunofluorescence and electron microscopy findings with clinical syndromes.
subtopics: Acute lesions: endothelial swelling, capillary wall thickening, fibrin thrombi, mesangiolysis and cortical necrosis
Subacute/chronic changes: double-contour GBM, onion-skin lesions, glomerulosclerosis and interstitial fibrosis
Tubular changes in ischemia and ATN
Immunofluorescence patterns in TMA and exclusion of immune complex diseases
Electron microscopy findings: endothelial injury, subendothelial widening and electron-dense deposits (when present)
Biopsy indications, sampling considerations and limitations
Correlation of histologic patterns with prognosis

chapters.title: Microbiology of Capnocytophaga canimorsus and Zoonotic Bacterial Infections
chapters.description: Biology, virulence factors, epidemiology and clinical spectrum of infections caused by Capnocytophaga species (emphasis on C. canimorsus) and general principles of zoonotic bacterial infections transmitted by dog and cat exposures.
subtopics: Classification and microbiology of Capnocytophaga species (gram-negative, fastidious, capnophilic rods)
Virulence determinants: capsule, sialidases, immune evasion strategies and serum susceptibility
Epidemiology and risk factors for invasive disease (bites, scratches, close contact; host factors like splenectomy or immunodeficiency)
Clinical syndromes: local wound infection, sepsis, meningitis, endocarditis and uncommon complications
Antimicrobial susceptibility patterns and empirical therapy considerations for animal bite–associated infections
Prevention of bite-related infections and wound management

chapters.title: Diagnostic Microbiology and Molecular Methods in Bloodstream Infections
chapters.description: Principles and practical aspects of diagnosing bacteremia: blood culture methodology, limitations of fastidious organisms, and the role of molecular diagnostics such as PCR and real-time sequencing technologies.
subtopics: Blood culture collection, media types (aerobic/anaerobic) and incubation dynamics
Factors affecting time-to-positivity and false negatives with fastidious organisms
Identification methods: biochemical testing, MALDI-TOF, 16S rRNA sequencing and whole-genome/nanopore approaches
Molecular tests for specific pathogens (PCR for Shiga toxin, pathogen-specific assays)
Turnaround times, sensitivity/specificity and interpretation in clinical context
When to pursue extended diagnostics for unusual pathogens

chapters.title: Pharmacology of Key Therapies: Antibiotics, Plasma Exchange and Complement Inhibitors
chapters.description: Mechanisms of action, indications, dosing considerations and adverse effects of antibiotics commonly used in animal-bite sepsis, principles and effects of plasma exchange, and pharmacology of monoclonal complement inhibitors (eg, eculizumab).
subtopics: Beta-lactam antibiotics: penicillin V, ampicillin, piperacillin/tazobactam — spectra, mechanisms, dose adjustments in renal failure
Principles of empiric and targeted antimicrobial therapy in zoonotic infections
Plasma exchange (plasmapheresis): mechanism, indications in TMA syndromes, replacement fluids (FFP, Octaplas), effects on drug levels and complement assays
Eculizumab and terminal complement blockade: mechanism (C5 inhibition), pharmacokinetics, dosing regimens, and monitoring
Risks and adverse effects: infection risk with complement inhibitors, infusion reactions
Drug interactions and special considerations (vaccination timing, prophylactic antibiotics)

chapters.title: Critical Care Management of Severe Sepsis and Dialysis-dependent AKI
chapters.description: Supportive care strategies in critically ill patients with sepsis and AKI, including hemodynamic management, indications for renal replacement therapy, and organ support modalities.
subtopics: Initial resuscitation: fluid strategy, vasopressor indications and choice
Management of septic cardiomyopathy and hemodynamic monitoring
Indications for renal replacement therapy (RRT) in AKI and modalities: intermittent hemodialysis vs continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT)
Practical aspects of CRRT: anticoagulation, dosing and fluid management
Glycemic control, nutrition, and prevention of ICU-related complications
Weaning from RRT and markers of renal recovery

chapters.title: Transfusion Medicine and Blood Product Support in Coagulopathy and Hemolysis
chapters.description: Indications, selection and risks of blood product transfusion in the setting of bleeding, coagulopathy and anemia; interactions with immunohematology testing and considerations in patients undergoing plasma exchange.
subtopics: Red blood cell transfusion thresholds and crossmatching considerations
Platelet transfusion indications and dosing
Plasma products: fresh frozen plasma, solvent-detergent pooled plasma (Octaplas) — uses and pros/cons
Fibrinogen replacement and cryoprecipitate
Impact of transfusion on serologic testing (DAT) and antigenicity
Transfusion-related complications: TRALI, TACO, alloimmunization, infection transmission

chapters.title: Vaccination and Infection Prophylaxis During Complement Inhibition
chapters.description: Rationale for vaccination and antimicrobial prophylaxis in patients receiving terminal complement inhibitors, recommended vaccines, timing around therapy, and strategies to mitigate meningococcal and other encapsulated organism risks.
subtopics: Impact of terminal complement blockade on susceptibility to encapsulated bacteria (Neisseria meningitidis, others)
Recommended vaccinations prior to complement inhibitor initiation: meningococcal conjugate and serogroup B vaccines, pneumococcal and Haemophilus influenzae considerations
Timing of vaccination relative to therapy and serologic response considerations
Antibiotic prophylaxis regimens when vaccines are not timely or in certain high-risk scenarios
Patient education about infection signs and emergency plans
Post-vaccination monitoring and reporting of adverse events

chapters.title: Approach to Pancytopenia and Multisystem Presentations
chapters.description: Systematic evaluation of patients with pancytopenia and multi-organ involvement, including differential diagnoses (infectious, hematologic, autoimmune, drug-induced), diagnostic algorithms and when to involve specialty services.
subtopics: Causes of pancytopenia: bone marrow failure, marrow infiltration, peripheral destruction/consumption, hypersplenism
Key laboratory and imaging investigations: peripheral smear, reticulocyte count, bone marrow examination, cultures and serologies
Distinguishing hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH), acute leukemia, aplastic anemia and sepsis-associated cytopenias
Role and timing of hematology consultation and bone marrow biopsy
Integration of clinical, laboratory and microbiologic data to prioritize management steps

chapters.title: Clinical Reasoning and Risk–Benefit Decision-making in Immunomodulatory Therapy During Infection
chapters.description: Frameworks for weighing risks and benefits when initiating immune-targeted therapies (eg, complement inhibitors, immunosuppression, plasma exchange) in patients with concurrent or recently treated infections.
subtopics: Principles of risk–benefit assessment in the presence of active infection
Timing considerations: when to delay, bridge therapies and criteria for safe initiation
Use of source control and antimicrobial stewardship in parallel with immunomodulation
Monitoring for infectious complications and mitigation strategies
Documentation, informed consent and multidisciplinary communication
Ethical considerations and guideline-based decision making
